To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) endocannabinoids potentiation by UBR597 and CB1 receptor antagonization by AM251 or D2 receptor antagonization by haloperidole had inhibitory effects on the response to food and/or novelty, and (2) the coadministration of URB597 and haloperidole restored the reward and reward-dependent behavior and CB1-mediated GABergic transmission only in the case of palatable food reward.
the endocannabinoid modulation of DAergic system has a stimulus-dependent effect on reward.
the ECS potentiation by UBR597 and the inhibition by AM251 of DAergic system are able to modulate the response toward reward.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interaction between ECS and DAergic transmission, and the effects of these systems on reward and reward-related behavior.
the interaction between the ECS and the DAergic system in the processes related to reward.

the interaction between endocannabinoids and dopamine, which is involved in the processes that mediate the responses to reward, and it is suggested that the endocannabinoid-mediated potentiation of dopamine release may contribute to the reward process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
endocannabinoid activation is necessary to obtain reward and that DAergic activity modulates reward-dependent behavior.
ECS potentiation and DAergic inhibition are both required for reward-dependent motor activity, which is dependent on the type of reward.
the endocannabinoid modulation of the response to reward is dependent on the DAergic transmission.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ECS activation and DAergic system inhibition are necessary for reward, but only when the reward is the palatable food.
the ECS is an important modulator of reward and reward-dependent behavior, but its effects are not always beneficial.
the ECS and DAergic systems have a bidirectional relationship and their interaction depends on the reward type.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ECS activation by URB597, alone or in presence of haloperidol, is able to potentiate the response toward palatable food.
the interaction between ECS and DAergic systems in the dorsomedial and dorsolateral striatum modulates the response to reward.
the interaction between endocannabinoids and DAergic systems in reward-related behavior is dependent on the type of stimulus used as a reward.
